messages:
Anna (Support): p1 escalation from ACME — they're seeing a huge uptick in 429s + increased latency after a marketing send. Customer says 50-70% of requests get 429s for /v1/generate. Token: acct-acme-prod. Happening since ~08:10 UTC. No recent changes on their side per customer. Can infra/sre help with attribution (route/model/customer) and quick mitigations?

Ryan (Infra): thx. quick Qs — is it sustained or bursts? window? any pattern on route/model? do we have request ids or example traces?

Anna (Support): mostly tight bursts following the campaign, last 40m had 3 big spikes. Example request-id: req_6f3b9a. Model seems to be red-opt-2.7b for most failing calls, route is /v1/generate. I pulled a few raw responses from the customer; they include rate limit headers (see below).

Anna (Support): sample 429 response headers from customer:
```
HTTP/1.1 429 Too Many Requests
x-rw-rate-limit: 60; min_remaining=0; window=60
x-rw-quota: tokens=1000000; used=842123; reset=1700000000
x-request-id: req_6f3b9a
content-type: application/json
```

Maria (SRE): useful. first steps for forensics: check 3 things in parallel — 1) 429 spike by customer_id, 2) 429 by route + model, 3) rate limiter internal metrics (bucket exhaustion, queue depth). PromQL snippets to run in Grafana/Prometheus:
```
sum by (customer_id) (increase(redwood_http_response_total{code="429"}[5m]))
sum by (route,model) (increase(redwood_http_response_total{code="429"}[15m]))
sum by (customer_id) (increase(redwood_tokens_consumed_total[1h]))
redwood_rate_limiter_burst_tokens{customer_id="acct-acme-prod"}
redwood_rate_limiter_rejected_total{reason="rate_limit"}
```

Maria (SRE): also check the runtime queue lengths and token cache thrashing:
```
redwood_runtime_queue_length{shard!=""}
redwood_kv_cache_hitrate{model="red-opt-2.7b"}
```

Ryan (Infra): adding a query for global per-route throttles — helps know if it's a global per-route capacity or per-tenant quota:
```
sum by(route) (increase(redwood_rate_limited_requests_total[5m]))
```

Anna (Support): customer provided a repro curl, sharing:
```
curl -v -H "Authorization: Bearer sk-acme-prod" -X POST https://api.redwood.com/v1/generate -d '{"input":"hello world","max_tokens":512}'
```

Zoe (Product): is this quota exhaustion (daily token quota) or the per-second burst window? we need to know which mitigation to offer (raise burst vs temporary quota top-up). what's current plan for acct-acme-prod?

Anna (Support): their plan: 1,000,000 tokens/day, burst allowance 10k/min (per-contract). They already used ~842k today per headers. But bursts would be allowed if burst credits exist. unsure if burst credits depleted.

Maria (SRE): ok — likely burst credit exhaustion causing 429s on minute windows. Steps: 1) verify burst token metric for acct-acme-prod (see redwood_rate_limiter_burst_tokens), 2) check whether 429s correlate with request concurrency or token-per-request (big requests chew tokens faster). Run:
```
sum by(customer_id) (increase(redwood_request_tokens_total[5m]))
sum by(customer_id) (increase(redwood_http_response_total{code="429"}[5m]))
```

Maria (SRE): quick mitigations we can do now (low-risk):
- Temporarily increase burst allowance for acct-acme-prod (multiply by 2) for 30m.
- Add a temporary route-specific soft-limit so their traffic can be degraded to a smaller model (e.g., route -> red-opt-1.3b) for heavy requests.
- Create an alert that notifies us when a single customer generates >50 429s in a 5m window.

Ryan (Infra): I can patch a rate-limit override. patch example in our config service:
```
PATCH /api/internal/rate-limits/acct-acme-prod
Content-Type: application/json
{ "burst_multiplier": 2, "ttl_seconds": 1800, "reason": "support mitigation - campaign spike" }
```
I’ll queue it and post back once applied.

DevBot (inc-bot): INC-1234 created by Anna — 429s for acct-acme-prod, priority P1.

Anna (Support): thanks @ryan — also requested that customer throttle down client concurrency while we triage; they agreed to backoff to 5rps.

Maria (SRE): attribution notes for the postmortem/dashboard: don't just show raw 429 counts — show 429 per-1k-requests and 429 per-10k-tokens, plus model-level breakdown. Suggested dashboard panels: 
- 429 rate heatmap by customer (5m bins)
- Top 10 customers by 429s and tokens consumed (timepicker: 1h/24h)
- Model-level throttle attribution (which model variants are causing most rejections)
- Latency p50/p95/p99 vs tokens_per_request for the failing timeframe
- Burst credit consumption over time per customer

Maria (SRE): saved PromQLs for the dashboard (copy/paste):
```
# 429s by customer
sum by(customer_id) (increase(redwood_http_response_total{code="429"}[5m]))

# 429s normalized by requests
( sum by(customer_id) (increase(redwood_http_response_total{code="429"}[5m])) ) /
( sum by(customer_id) (increase(redwood_http_response_total[5m])) )

# tokens per request distribution
histogram_quantile(0.95, sum(rate(redwood_request_size_tokens_bucket[5m])) by (le, customer_id))
```

Zoe (Product): for billing/CS — need a clear note on whether this was contract limit enforcement vs infra saturation. If it's strictly a quota, we should authorize a one-time top-up and advise customer on best practices (client-side backoff, jitter, exponential).

Anna (Support): I'll draft customer communication: explain burst credit depletion, offer temporary top-up or route downgrade, include suggested client changes (exponential backoff, token size reduction).

Ryan (Infra): override applied. burst_multiplier=2 for acct-acme-prod, expires in 30m. I also enabled a temporary diagnostic trace sampling for their requests (sample_rate=0.5) to catch traces.

Maria (SRE): after override, watch these charts: 429s by customer, rate_limiter_rejected_total, and runtime queue depth. If 429s drop but latency stays high, we might be hitting runtime CPU/kv-cache pressure not rate limits.

Anna (Support): customer reports 429s reduced to ~5% of previous and latencies improved. They accepted a postmortem + dashboard link. I'll keep the ticket open until we confirm no regressions.

Maria (SRE): action items:
- (SRE) create a saved dashboard view "Limit Forensics — customer attribution" with the panels above.
- (Infra) verify burst token accounting and confirm if quota resets as expected.
- (Support/Product) add guidance to the plan docs about burst behavior and recommended backoff parameters.

Zoe (Product): also add a small note to billing: when we do temporary top-ups we should bill pro-rata or mark as one-time credit. I can coordinate.

DevBot (inc-bot): INC-1234 updated: mitigated, monitoring.

Anna (Support): closing loop — will post the dashboard link + short postmortem in #support once available. thanks all :white_check_mark:
